_seed_meta.description: Identifies all activities requiring written agency approval on federal awards. Extracts budget changes, equipment purchases, PI changes, and foreign travel requirements into a trackable reference document.

items.name: Prior Approval Requirements Tracking
items.description: Identify and to track all activities requiring federal agency prior approval to prevent compliance violations

data.prompt:
You are analyzing a Federal Award Notice/Agreement document. Extract ALL prior approval requirements to create a comprehensive tracking system for activities requiring federal agency authorization.
Thoroughly search the entire document for prior approval requirements. Pay special attention to sections referencing:

"Prior Approval"
"Pre-approval"
"Written Approval"
"Agency Approval"
"2 CFR 200" sections
"Research Terms and Conditions" (RTCs)

Create a comprehensive response with these sections:

BUDGET-RELATED PRIOR APPROVALS:

Re-budgeting thresholds and restrictions
Equipment purchases requiring approval
Subcontracting/subaward approvals
Cost sharing changes
Personnel effort modifications


SCOPE & TIMELINE APPROVALS:

Scope of work changes
Principal Investigator changes
Key personnel changes
No-cost extension requests
Performance site changes


ADMINISTRATIVE APPROVALS:

Foreign travel approvals
Conference/meeting expenditures
Participant support costs
Property acquisition or disposition
Intellectual property arrangements


APPROVAL PROCEDURES:
Create a table with:

Approval Type
Threshold/Trigger
Required Documentation
Approval Authority
Processing Timeline
Consequences of Non-compliance


WAIVED APPROVALS:

Research Terms and Conditions (RTC) waivers
Agency-specific approval delegations
Streamlined approval processes



Be thorough. Search for keywords: 'prior approval,' 'pre-approval,' 'written approval,' 'agency approval,' 'permission,' 'authorize,' 'CFR 200,' 'RTC,' 'waive,' 'delegate,' 'threshold.'
If information is not found for any section, explicitly state 'Not specified in the document' rather than omitting the section. Please be 100% accurate.

You are a document formatting specialist. Take the provided Prior Approval Requirements analysis output and reformat it for maximum readability while preserving ALL information exactly as provided.

FORMATTING REQUIREMENTS:
1. Keep all section headers bolded with ** markdown
2. Convert each bullet point category to bold format: **Category Name:** 
3. Maintain all original content word-for-word after the colon
4. Convert the APPROVAL PROCEDURES section to a proper markdown table with borders
5. Preserve the exact same structure and order for all other sections
6. Do not add, remove, or modify any substantive information
7. Use consistent bullet formatting throughout

INPUT FORMAT EXAMPLE:
* Re-budgeting thresholds and restrictions: Not specified in the document.

OUTPUT FORMAT REQUIRED:
* **Re-budgeting thresholds and restrictions:** Not specified in the document.

TABLE FORMATTING REQUIREMENTS:
- Convert the APPROVAL PROCEDURES section to this exact markdown table format:
- Must include the header separator row with dashes
- Use proper markdown table syntax with | separators

REQUIRED TABLE FORMAT:
| Approval Type | Threshold/Trigger | Required Documentation | Approval Authority | Processing Timeline | Consequences of Non-compliance |
|---------------|-------------------|------------------------|-------------------|---------------------|-------------------------------|
| [data] | [data] | [data] | [data] | [data] | [data] |

TRANSFORMATION RULES:
- Change: * Category name: content
- To: * **Category name:** content
- Keep all section headers exactly as they are
- Maintain all "Not specified in the document" statements exactly
- Preserve any detailed information exactly as written
- Do not summarize, paraphrase, or alter any content
- For APPROVAL PROCEDURES: Extract each row of data and format as proper markdown table with header separators

Apply this formatting transformation to the entire provided Prior Approval Requirements analysis output. The goal is enhanced readability through consistent bolding and proper table formatting with visible borders while maintaining 100% information fidelity

validation_plan.name: Figures match the source
validation_plan.description: Every threshold, percentage, dollar amount and day count in the output appears in the source document with the same value, unit and (for dates) year. A figure the output calculated says how it was calculated and the arithmetic is right. FAIL if any value differs from the source, or appears with no basis in it.

validation_plan.name: Every prior-approval requirement is listed
validation_plan.description: Each activity the award says needs prior written approval (rebudgeting, equipment, PI or key personnel change, effort reduction, foreign travel, no-cost extension, subawards) is listed with its threshold or timing as stated. FAIL for each requirement omitted.

validation_plan.name: Says when the document is silent
validation_plan.description: For each approval requirement or procedure that the source document does not state, the output says it is not stated (or not found) instead of filling in a typical value, a common practice or a figure from memory, and instead of leaving it out without comment. FAIL if a missing item is given a value the document does not contain.

validation_inputs.label: Fictional notice of award. Answer key: award EXA-2027-0412; project period July 1, 2027 to June 30, 2029; budget period 1 July 1, 2027 to June 30, 2028; this action $250,000 ($200,000 direct, $50,000 indirect); total anticipated $510,000; indirect 25% of MTDC; no cost sharing; annual progress report and SF-425 due 90 days after each budget period (September 28, 2028 for period 1); final reports and invention statement due 120 days after the project end (October 28, 2029); prior approval for a PI change, foreign travel, rebudgeting participant support, equipment over $10,000 per item, and a PI effort reduction over 25%; one no-cost extension, requested at least 10 days before the end (by June 20, 2029); records kept 3 years from the final SF-425. Not stated: a data management plan requirement.
validation_inputs.text:
FICTIONAL QA MATERIAL — NOT A REAL AWARD
Notice of Award — Example Science Agency
Award Number: EXA-2027-0412
Federal Award Identification Number (FAIN): EXA20270412
Recipient: Example State University
Principal Investigator: Jordan Sample
Project Title: Watershed Sensor Network Pilot
Project period: July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2029
Budget period 1: July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028
Amount of this action (budget period 1): $250,000, of which direct costs $200,000 and indirect costs $50,000.
Total anticipated award for both budget periods, subject to the availability of funds: $510,000.
Indirect costs: 25% of modified total direct costs (MTDC), per the recipient's negotiated rate agreement dated March 3, 2026.
Cost sharing: none required.

Reporting
- An annual progress report is due 90 days after the end of each budget period.
- An annual Federal Financial Report (SF-425) is due 90 days after the end of each budget period.
- The final progress report, final SF-425 and final invention statement are due 120 days after the end of the project period.

Prior approval
Prior written approval from the agency is required for (a) a change of principal investigator, (b) foreign travel, and (c) rebudgeting of participant support costs.
Equipment purchases over $10,000 per item require prior approval.
The principal investigator commits 1.2 calendar months per year; a reduction of more than 25% requires prior approval.
One no-cost extension may be requested, at least 10 days before the end of the project period.

Records
Records must be kept for 3 years from the date the final SF-425 is submitted.
